resources.string: "Allow cache access, then scan your apps."
"Android manages cache. Clearing it does not guarantee a faster phone."

"This is an experimental cache cleaner. Android does not let us delete other apps\' cache directly. With your permission, the cleaning helper opens each selected app in Settings and taps Clear cache.\n\nNo app-data deletion, ads or internet access. STOP stays visible. Unknown screens are skipped. Cache can grow back immediately; a large cache does not necessarily make your phone slow."
"Android shows the cleaning helper as on, but it is not connected. Switch Ultra1TapCache off and on in Accessibility, then return here. Cleaning never starts by itself.\n\n"

"The cleaning helper needs Android Accessibility access. Open Settings, choose Ultra1TapCache and turn it on. Return here and tap Clean when you are ready. Nothing starts automatically.

It only opens app settings and taps Clear cache. STOP stays visible. No internet access.

If Android blocks the switch: App info > menu > Allow restricted settings (if offered), then enable the helper."
"Settings report allowed, but Android denies cache access"

"

Open Usage access for Ultra1TapCache. If it is already allowed, switch it off and on. Returning here scans again automatically.

If the switch is blocked: App info > menu > Allow restricted settings (only if offered). If access still fails, restart the phone and share this diagnostic with the Usage access screen. You do not need to reinstall."
"Open Settings > Special app access > Usage access manually."
"Your apps will appear here after a scan."
"No cache found in the scanned apps. Turn on Show apps with no cache to see them."
"The scan is still running. Wait for it to finish before cleaning."
"Select an app with cache, or scan again first."
"\nCheck the cleaning helper and try again."
"Only cache will be cleared, not app data. STOP stays on screen. Unknown settings screens are skipped. Please leave Settings alone while cleaning is running."
"\nCache total unavailable. Only this app can be measured."
"\nTap Allow cache access for help and details."
"\nCleaning helper is on but not connected."
"\nSet up the cleaning helper before cleaning."
"STOP is unavailable. Cleaning was not started."
"Only during cleaning you start: opens Android app settings and taps Clear cache. No app-data deletion, ads or internet access. Unknown screens are skipped. You can stop at any time."

"Only allow this if you trust the app. Accessibility can read your screen and interact with apps.

1. Tap Open app info below.
2. Open the three-dot menu at the top.
3. Choose Allow restricted settings, if Android offers it, and follow its instructions.
4. Return here, enable Usage access and the cleaning helper, then scan again.

No menu option? It may already be allowed or this Android version uses a different path. Open Accessibility first and tap the blocked switch to read Android's guidance. We cannot bypass the restriction or remove it automatically."
"This also selects apps supplied with your phone, such as Chrome. Only enabled apps with measured cache are selected. This does not start cleaning. You can deselect any app afterwards."
"Confirmed apps are skipped for this saved run. Remaining apps are measured again before any tap. This may retry unconfirmed apps. STOP stays visible. Cleaning only starts when you tap Resume."
"Could not resume. Check the cleaning helper. If cache measurement timed out, turn the helper off and on before trying again."
"Android cache measurement did not respond. Progress saved. Reconnect the cleaning helper before resuming."
"Cleaning stopped due to an error. Progress saved"
"Previous run was interrupted outside the app. Exact cause unknown. Progress saved"
First, allow usage access so the app can measure cache. Tap Open settings and enable Ultra1TapCache. Come back here for the next step.

Next, enable the cleaning helper in Accessibility settings. If Android says restricted settings, open App info, tap the three dots and allow restricted settings if offered. Then return to Accessibility settings. Android requires you to make the final permission choice yourself.

Android may restrict this installation. The install source is outside Google Play or unknown, and the cleaning helper is not enabled. This is a hint, not proof that a restriction is active.

1. Tap Open app info below.
2. Tap the three dots.
3. If offered, choose Allow restricted settings and follow Android's instructions. Only do this if you trust this app: accessibility access can read the screen and interact with other apps.
4. Come back and enable the cleaning helper in Accessibility settings.

If the menu item is absent, continue with normal setup. Nothing is enabled automatically.
